rundown: England beat New Zealand 37-12 at Allianz Stadium in London, England. England led 56-17 at the half and never looked back.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 21, 9:07 AM ET. It had New Zealand 21% and England 79%, projecting New Zealand 26.7 – England 39.7 (66.5 total, England by 13).

Final: New Zealand 12 – England 37. Right winner: it had England at 79%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
New Zealand came in with a 22% above average attack and a 2% stingier than average defense (LWWWL, 38.4 scored and 25.2 allowed a game over 5 games), worth about 12 and 12 games of evidence. Projected to score 26.7, they scored 12 (−14.7 points, 55% under); projected to allow 39.7, they allowed 37 (−2.7 points, 7% under).

England came in with a 45% above average attack and a 6% stingier than average defense (WWWWL, 49.6 scored and 22.8 allowed a game over 5 games), worth about 12 and 12 games of evidence. Projected to score 39.7, they scored 37 (−2.7 points, 7% under); projected to allow 26.7, they allowed 12 (−14.7 points, 55% under).

The bigger miss was New Zealand's scoring (-14.7 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 49 against 66.5 projected (-17.5), about the 12th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15).

Margin: England by 25 against England by 13 projected, about the 77th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±16).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Form (NZL 3-2 L5 · ENG 4-1 L5): England ×1.03, New Zealand ×1.01. It favored England, who did beat their projection by more than the other side did.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; there were no odds to check the projection against.

The result was off its normal range without being an outlier, so the flags may have played a part.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.739 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +12 points. It counts toward Rugby scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 21 graded Rugby games the algo now scales scoring ×0.994 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: New Zealand attack ×0.966, defense ×1.008 (3 games); England attack ×1.040, defense ×0.960 (3 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
